LOCK RULING: lockpicking keeps NO probability roll. Deterministic ward-collar -- N wards per tier (1..5), collar rotates 90 deg/s, tolerance W = clamp(4 + 0.55*(Security - req_tier), 4, 34) degrees, 3 sweeps per ward, a press outside W breaks one pick and makes an 11m/+55 alert sound. Below the tier's Security OR AGILITY requirement the interaction is not offered at all. Argument: a retryable roll is not a gate, it is a tax on time (12%/attempt = 100% after ~8 attempts); a roll destroys RI-PRG03's five-tier Security table; RI-PRG03 method 7 already rules gates deterministic so ruling otherwise would re-litigate a decided seam.

PROPOSED SEAM S20 (proposed in reply, NOT written to ARBITRATION.md): 'Keep the die where failure is permanent; delete it where failure is a retry.' Explains why RI-DLG04 persuasion keeps its roll (disposition lost permanently, non-retryable) while lockpicking loses its, and governs the deterministic jail skill loss in RI-CRM01 §6.

Morag Tong problem solved by jurisdictional legality: 4 sanctioning authorities (Morag Tong writ / Imperial Warrant of Attainder / ku-vastei Ruling / Wet Ledger report-interception), ZERO of which cover all three jurisdictions, max 2 holdable simultaneously (>=8 mutually exclusive faction pairs). 27 sanctioned-murder quests, 18 (67%) with a non-lethal option per S13. Morag Tong is deliberately the weakest: contact only, no rank, writs legally worthless in Argonia, honoured only socially by RG-DRES.

Bounty persistence (S6 specified): bounty, blood-price, unreported witness records, stolen_from, corpse death_flags and RI-STL01's S-4 zone alert ALL survive death, respawn and save round-trip. Only guard AGGRO resets. Special case: dying to a guard mid-arrest wakes you in jail with the sentence already running, not at your sapwell.

S10 handled explicitly: killing a witness before their report lands suppresses the bounty completely, with zero hidden penalty. The cost is a permanently dead named NPC (S5), faction rolls, and a corpse that is evidence. Required content: >=6 NPC lines and >=2 quest stages conditioned on a settlement's unexplained-death count, so a murder spree is something the world can talk about.
